name: Gurgani
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Borjian, Habib. 2008. The Extinct Language of Gurgan: Its Sources and Origins. Journal of the American Oriental Society 128(4): 681-707 (author deposit in Columbia Academic Commons, doi:10.7916/D8J68SQ1).
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. VII 'Notes on the transcription and phonology' (p.690) states the vowels themselves are unrecoverable from the Persian-orthography manuscripts ('The Gurgani vowels remain obscure..'); sec. VIII 'Historical phonology' is segmental correspondences only; the words stress/accent/prosody do not occur in the paper.

sources.citation: Bosworth, C. E. 2002. 'GORGAN vi. History from the rise of Islam to the beginning of the Safavid period.' Encyclopaedia Iranica XI/2: 153-154.
Kia (Kiya), Mohammad Sadeq. 1330 S/1951. Vazhe-name-ye Gorgani [A Gorgani vocabulary]. Tehran: Daneshgah-e Tehran. c.350 pp. In Persian.
sources.note: Nothing. Appendix 2 'Yaddashti dar bare-ye vaj-shenasi-ye guyesh-e Gorgani' (pp.247-252, read as page scan) is a list of 24 letter/sound correspondences between Gorgani spellings and Persian; Appendix 3 (pp.253ff) is grammar. No mention of takye (stress) found in the scanned text or on the pages viewed.
Nothing; cites only Borjian 2008 and Glottolog.

sources.citation: Bakhtiary, Arman (بختیاری، آرمان). 2020 (1399 S). بررسی پیوندهای زبانی میان پهلوی اشکانی و نوشته‌هایی از گویش گرگانی [Investigation of language relationships between Parthian and Gurgâni texts of Hurufiyye]. زبان پژوهی Zabanpazhuhi (Journal of Language Research, Alzahra University, Tehran) 12(35). In Persian, English abstract. ISSN 2008-8833 / 2538-1989.

tone.summary: Historical-comparative article (Parthian vs Gurgani); phonology is segmental only (7 vowels a ā e ē i o u, consonant correspondences). no prosody content.

sources.citation: Borjian, Habib. 2005. Review of Sadeqi 2001. Archiv Orientalni 73: 383-387.
